speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the appearance of your skin lesions, specifically their size, color, and whether they are changing over time? Have you noticed any bleeding, itching, or pain associated with them?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that detailed history. Given your age, smoking history, and the description of non-healing, crusty lesions in both sun-exposed (finger) and non-sun-exposed (penis) areas, we need to rule out malignancy immediately. Have you noticed any regional lymph nodes swelling in your groin or on your hand?

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, HIV status, and Syphilis serology (RPR/TPHA).
REQUEST IMAGES: Please provide clinical photos of the penile and digital lesions.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (penis and finger) until proven otherwise.
